thread:
PagerDuty: [INCIDENT] hosted-runtime-kvcache memory surge detected -> OOM risk (priority: P1)
OpsBot: paging oncall @Samir (primary) -> see alerts: hosted-runtime-*-kvcache mem > 85% across multiple hosts, OOM events on host-47/host-52.
Samir: acked. investigating. starting with kvcache metrics and recent deploys.
Samir: repeating what I see: kv_map_count spiked from ~12k -> 1.2M in ~8m, mem usage jumped from 40% -> 92% on runtimes serving hosted tier. continuous-batching inflight tokens also spiked.
Maya: I see the same in traces. Correlated with a deploy at 10:41 (rev: runtime-v2.18.3) that enabled prefetch sharding change.
Devon: tagging the deploy: infra/deploys#2389 set PREFETCH_SHARD_COUNT=16 and bumped default max_batch_window_ms to 1200.
Samir: suspecting prefix-amplification from long prompts + prefetch expansion + large batch window -> kv map explosion.
Samir: quick check logs on one pod:
```
$ kubectl -n hosted-runtime logs kvcache-47f -c runtime | tail -n 60
2026-03-15T10:47:12Z INF kvcache: prefetched_keys=10432 active_sessions=312
2026-03-15T10:47:12Z INF kvcache: kv_map_size=1189472
2026-03-15T10:47:13Z ERR runtime: OOM allocating 128MB
2026-03-15T10:47:13Z INF runtime: evicting session=acct:bookly-prod:session:...
2026-03-15T10:47:15Z INF batching: window_ms=1200 inflight_tokens=32000
```
Samir: command I ran to inspect kvmaps across hosts:
```
$ infractl kvcache dump --env hosted --summary | jq '.hosts[] | {host,kv_map_size,prefetch_rate}'
{ "host": "host-47", "kv_map_size": "1.19M", "prefetch_rate": "10.4k/s" }
{ "host": "host-52", "kv_map_size": "980k", "prefetch_rate": "9.8k/s" }
```
Maya: customers hitting long-context (>=50k tokens) started trending up after feature flags flip; looks like some clients sent multipart prompts that normalized into lots of unique prefixes.
Devon: quick mitigation options: 1) disable prefetch runtime-wide (flip feature flag) 2) reduce PREFETCH_SHARD_COUNT to 4 3) shrink max_batch_window_ms to 50 4) evict large sessions proactively.
Samir: doing option 1 + 3 as a hotpatch: disabling prefetch and lowering batch window to 50ms to reduce accumulation. Will apply to hosted-runtime kvcache service as a config patch and restart one replica at a time.
Samir: patch command (applied):
```
$ infractl feature-flag set hosted PREFETCH_ENABLED false --by=oncall-samir --note "emergency disable to stop kv growth"
$ infractl service config set hosted-runtime kvcache.max_batch_window_ms=50 kvcache.max_prefetch_per_request=32 --apply
$ infractl rollout restart service/hosted-runtime -w
```
OpsBot: rollout started: hosted-runtime -> restart rolling across 12 pods (maxUnavailable=2)
Samir: monitoring memory after first two pods restarted: host-47 mem dropped 40% -> 62% within 90s, no new OOMs so far.
Leo: I see request error rate dropped from 5.2% -> 0.8% after the flag flip for affected hosts. Latency P95 improved 500ms -> 120ms.
Maya: confirming kvcache kv_map_size is trending down: host-47 1.19M -> 270k over 6m. continuous-batching inflight tokens dropped accordingly.
Devon: note: we still have lingering large session entries - evicting aggressively might cause client-facing regressions. prefer to let GC/eviction run while keeping prefetch off.
Samir: running eviction probe on non-prod first, then we can nudge eviction in prod if needed.
Samir: immediate customer impact assessment:
- Affected customers: acct:acme-corp (prod), acct:bookly-prod (prod), acct:edu-dl (staging->prod traffic spike), several sandbox customers spiking.
- Symptom: intermittent 500/502/504 for hosted inference calls; error spike ~05:10-05:55 UTC during surge (peak at 5.2% of total hosted requests).
- Duration: active surge ~20m, residual elevated mem for ~45m.
- Business impact: increased latencies and transient failures for small subset of hosted customers using long-context prompts. No Dedicated or Private clusters affected.
Maya: alerted account teams for acme-corp and bookly-prod, message sent to #customer-notifications draft: "We're investigating intermittent errors; mitigation applied; follow-up postmortem to be shared."
Devon: adding short-term observability guard: alert kvcache_kvmap_size > 200k for hosted nodes with exponential growth over 5m -> page. Also added a runbook link.
Samir: paging notes / timeline to handoff:
- 10:41 deploy (runtime-v2.18.3) enabled PREFETCH_SHARD_COUNT=16 and batch window=1200 ms
- 10:46 kv_map growth begins, mem climbs -> OOMs by 10:47
- 10:48 PagerDuty triggered, oncall paged
- 10:50 hotpatch initiated (PREFETCH_ENABLED=false + batch window=50)
- 10:54 first pods restart; mem falls, OOMs stop by 10:55
- 11:10 rollout complete and metrics stable for ~15m
Samir: checklist for next oncall (please confirm before clearing):
- Keep PREFETCH_ENABLED=false until postmortem and safe rollout plan (owner: Devex/Runtime)
- Monitor kvcache_kvmap_size, mem, and inflight_tokens for at least 2h (dashboard: infra/hosted/kvcache/oom)
- Re-enable prefetch only after we have: a) sharding changes validated in canary with short batch window, b) prefix deduping heuristics landed, c) throttles per-account implemented.
Anika: @Samir adding action items to INC-2026-291234 and assigning owners: Devon (runtime config), Maya (customer comms), Leo (metrics/alerts), Samir (postmortem owner).
Samir: offloading raw logs and diagnostic snapshot to incident artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/2912340000/ (kvcache dumps, pod logs, infractl outputs).
Maya: customer outreach: sent targeted note to acme-corp & bookly-prod via CSM. request for status: they confirm errors saw at 10:47-10:55 and are back to normal.
Leo: quick retrospective note: root cause appears to be a combination of (A) prefetch expansion + (B) large batch window amplifying unique prefix keys and (C) lack of an early-growth guard on kvmap size.
Devon: long term fixes proposed: 1) prefix dedupe + compacting prefetch keys 2) default prefetch cap per-account 3) lower safe default batch window 4) mem-based circuit breaker for kvcache that disables prefetch on growth.
Samir: for the postmortem timeline, I'll capture exact metric deltas and attach logs. planning 90-min blameless postmortem tomorrow 1500 UTC.
Anika: handing off to next oncall @Leo. please confirm system stable for 30m before clearing page.
Leo: confirmed. will monitor dashboards for 60m and post status. leaving note: PREFETCH_ENABLED=false, rollout version pinned to runtime-v2.18.2 behavior for prefetch.
Samir: thanks team. great quick work. :thumbsup: :tada:
PagerDuty: incident status -> mitigated. next steps: postmortem, config hardening, deployment gating for prefetch changes.
Leo: closing remarks to handoff: watch for any customer reopenings; keep contact list handy. created follow-up ticket: INC-2026-291234-POSTMORTEM.
Maya: adding retrospective action: add canary metric for kv_map_size growth rate and a synthetic long-context test to CI to catch prefix amplification regressions.
Devon: I'll prepare a safe rollout plan for PREFETCH_SHARD_COUNT and batch window with canary and AB tests.
Anika: noted. I will update the incident channel with postmortem link once available.
Samir: clearing from active page at 11:25 UTC, handing to Leo.
Leo: ack. monitoring...
